properties.description: Chromium nitride with nickel powder (duplicate label)

nodes.name: CrNN Synthesis on Ni Foam
nodes.procedure: The catalyst was synthesized by hydrolysis of precursors at 90°C, drop-drying the product to coat a Ni foam followed by annealing at 300°C (see the Supporting Information). We intentionally added Ni powder during drop drying of reaction precursors into a Ni foam.

unit_operations.name: Drop-drying
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: drop-drying the product to coat a Ni foam

nodes.source_text: The catalyst was synthesized by hydrolysis of precursors at 90°C, drop-drying the product to coat a Ni foam followed by annealing at 300°C (see the Supporting Information).

nodes.name: NiO/Ni Heterostructure Synthesis
nodes.procedure: We recently showed that a Ni/NiO core-shell heterostructure affording similar activity as Pt for hydrogen-evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysis.
nodes.source_text: We recently showed that a Ni/NiO core-shell heterostructure affording similar activity as Pt for hydrogen-evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysis.

nodes.description: HER LSV performance comparison in 1M KOH
nodes.source_text: In 1M KOH, the CrNN electrocatalyst showed zero overpotential at the HER onset and 150mV overpotential to reach a current density of 100mAcm⁻² without iR compensation, which is similar to commercial Pt/C under similar loading (Figure 2a).
10% Cr₂O₃ greatly stabilized the catalyst with an initially increasing current density through an activation phase over 48h and a stable current density afterwards (Figure 2b).
NiO/Ni electrocatalyst showed a gradual decrease in current density suggesting catalyst degradation

nodes.description: HER LSV optimized with Ni powder addition
nodes.source_text: An optimal loading of 24mgcm⁻² CrNN catalyst with 30wt% Ni powder in Ni foam could yield a current density of 100mAcm⁻² at an overpotential of 115mV without iR compensation (Figure 2c inset).

nodes.description: HER chronoamperometry stability at constant -0.25V vs RHE
nodes.source_text: the catalyst also exhibited stable behavior in maintaining current density over 200mAcm⁻² for at least 80h at -250mV versus RHE without iR compensation (Figure 2c).

nodes.description: Two-electrode alkaline electrolyzer OWS at RT (23°C)
nodes.source_text: At room temperature (RT, 23°C), the electrolyzer impressively delivered a water splitting current at an onset voltage of 1.46V, and a high current density of 200mA cm⁻² at 1.75V without iR compensation (1.57 V with iR compensation; Figure 4b).

nodes.description: Two-electrode electrolyzer chronopotentiometry stability at 20mA/cm² RT
nodes.source_text: The electrolyzer was stable at a current density of 20mAcm⁻² under a nearly constant voltage of 1.50V (without iR compensation) over 500h (Figure 4c).

nodes.description: Solar-driven water splitting with GaAs cells under AM1.5
nodes.source_text: By connecting our electrolyzer with two GaAs solar cells in series... we were able to produce a high current density of 12.10mAcm⁻² (Figure 4d) corresponding to a solar-to-hydrogen efficiency of 14.9% under AM1.5 100mWcm⁻² assuming a faradaic efficiency of 100%.

nodes.description: Two-electrode electrolyzer chronopotentiometry stability at 200mA/cm² RT
nodes.source_text: It also showed negligible decay under a high current density of 200mAcm⁻² for 50h under 1.75V and 1.64V at RT and 60°C, respectively (Figure 4c).
It also showed negligible decay under a high current density of 200mAcm⁻² for 50h under 1.75V and 1.64V at RT and 60°C, respectively (Figure 4c).

nodes.description: Two-electrode alkaline electrolyzer OWS LSV at 60°C
nodes.source_text: At 60°C, the curves shifted by 100mV to lower voltages with a 1.39V onset potential and 1.64V at the current density of 200mA cm⁻².

nodes.description: Long-term HER stability test for structural analysis at -60mV vs RHE
nodes.source_text: the CrNN catalyst showed negligible particle oxidation with an almost intact NiO/Ni core structure after 48h electrolysis operation at -60mV versus reversible hydrogen electrode... slightly increased electrochemical surface area by 1.23 times for the CrNN electrocatalyst.

nodes.description: Long-term HER stability test for structural analysis
nodes.source_text: The NiO/Ni heterostructures without any Cr added showed significant particle oxidation into larger NiO aggregates over 24h HER operation.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images showed well-coated Ni wires in the Ni foam by a film of highly dispersed nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images showed well-coated Ni wires in the Ni foam by a film of highly dispersed nanoparticles (Figure 1a)

properties.description: High-magnification view of porous, trabecular-like nanostructure with red square ROI

nodes.characterization_summary: AES elemental mapping showed uniform distribution of Ni, O, and Cr elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: in which Auger electron spectroscopy (AES) mapping suggested a uniform distribution of Ni, O, and Cr elements (Figure 1a)

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM imaging showed 5-20 nm nanoparticles of CrNN catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: With the catalyst nanoparticles sonicated off from the Ni foam, scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) imaging showed 5-20 nm nanoparticles (Figure 1b and Figure S1)

properties.description: Grayscale TEM micrograph showing nanoparticle lattice fringes

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-EELS mapping revealed 3-10 nm metallic Ni cores coated by 1-2 nm thick NiOx layer partitioned by 1-2 nm CrOx domains showing Cr2O3-blended NiO/Ni heterostructures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Atomic scale electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) mapping... revealed 3-10 nm metallic Ni cores coated by a 1-2 nm thick layer of nickel oxide (NiOx) partitioned by 1-2 nm chromium oxide (CrOx) domains (Figure 1c-f)

nodes.characterization_summary: Depth profiling XPS confirmed +2 and +3 oxidation states of Ni and Cr respectively in the oxide layer, and inner metallic Ni core after Ar sputtering.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Depth profiling X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) further confirmed the +2 and +3 oxidation states of Ni and Cr, respectively, in the oxide layer, and the inner metallic Ni core when the oxide layer was removed by in situ Ar sputtering (Figure S2)

nodes.characterization_summary: NiO/Ni heterostructure showed severe oxidation of metallic Ni into larger NiO aggregates after stability test.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The NiO/Ni heterostructures without any Cr added showed significant particle oxidation into larger NiO aggregates over 24 h HER operation (Figure 3a and b)

nodes.characterization_summary: CrNN catalyst showed negligible particle oxidation with almost intact NiO/Ni core structure after 48 h electrolysis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the CrNN catalyst showed negligible particle oxidation with an almost intact NiO/Ni core structure after 48 h electrolysis operation at -60 mV versus reversible hydrogen electrode (Figure 3d and e)

nodes.characterization_summary: CV curves (second cycle, 10 mV/s) showed Ni2+/Niδ+ (δ≥3) redox peak area increase by 1.23 times after 48 h HER for CrNN (larger ECSA) vs decrease for NiO/Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Cyclic voltammetry curves (second cycle) of the CrNN catalyst before and after stability test at a scan rate of 10 mVs−1 in 1 M KOH, showing the formation of an oxidation-resistant Ni species... By comparing the peak areas of Ni2+/Niδ+ (δ≥3) redox peak before and after 48 h of HER reaction, we observed a slightly increased electrochemical surface area by 1.23 times for the CrNN electrocatalyst (Figure 3f)

nodes.characterization_summary: Intact NiO/Ni chemical property confirmed after stability test.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The intact NiO/Ni chemical property was further confirmed by XPS analysis (Figure S4)
